source.title: Do Large Language Models Have Compositional Ability? An Investigation into Limitations and Scalability
source.authors: Zhuoyan Xu; Zhenmei Shi; Ying-Yu Liang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures exact-match accuracy on in-context composite tasks across model sizes. This bears on downstream performance versus scale, but it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. when discussing scaling laws, but reports no held-out pretraining cross-entropy, parameter/token/compute loss fits, extrapolation tests, or compute-optimal allocation experiments. Rows below cover composite-task accuracy reported by model size. The other simple-task and composite-in-context accuracy results are not included: they are comparison settings rather than the composite-task outcome used here.
record.test_reason: The study reports exact-match accuracy on synthetic in-context composite tasks for public Mistral, Llama1/2/3 and GPT families across model sizes (Table 4, Table 6, Figures 2–4). This bears on V6 (downstream performance vs scale) in a new setting. Scale is not controlled: families differ in data and training, and Mistral 8x7B is a mixture-of-experts model. Nothing is measured on pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested. T3 rather than T2: the paper studies compositional ability and treats scale as a secondary axis.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that separable composite tasks show decent compositional ability that improves with scale. Tasks needing sequential multi-step reasoning underperform, and scaling generally gives no improvement. Composite in-context examples let models solve the composite tasks. A linear-attention theory backs the separability account.
record.recipe_differences: This is an in-context learning evaluation on synthetic composite tasks, using exact-match accuracy across model sizes; it does not fit pretraining loss scaling laws or vary training compute, tokens, or parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with task structure (separable versus sequential), task domain (logical versus linguistic), model family and scale, and whether demonstrations are simple-task or composite-task examples.

fits_no_version.finding: In a one-layer linear self-attention model, lower rank of the attention matrices (a proxy for scale) lowers the upper bound on composite accuracy for confined-support tasks (Theorem 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Theoretical account of why downstream compositional accuracy scales only for separable tasks.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed accuracy results. The evidence concerns a bespoke synthetic in-context composite-task suite, not held-out pretraining loss or conventional downstream benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 reports nine additional composite accuracy results for (A)+(C), Capitalization & Two Sum, one for each listed Mistral, Llama2 and Llama1 model size. These nine rows are omitted to prioritize the task conditions used to characterize scaling behavior and the additional Llama3 results in Table 6.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes.
Performance as a function of pretraining loss; whether gains are predictable (no curve fits); and controlled scaling within one training recipe. Only public checkpoints are compared.

missing.what: Word error rate vs model size on linguistic composite tasks (T1 PhraReco+LongChain, T2 Passive-Active+Object-Subject). WER improves with scale, especially for Llama2.
Capitalization & Swap composite accuracy vs scale for the GPT family (0.74B–6B) and OpenLlama 3B; composite stays at about 20% or below.

record.verdict_notes: Scale comparisons span public model families with different training data and architectures, so they are not controlled scaling. Values are three-run averages on 100 test examples, with no uncertainty reported. (A)+(C) rows are declared left out; they show gains with Llama2 scale (3→44%) but Llama1 65B drops to 2%.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating held-out loss from smaller runs to larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests accuracy on synthetic in-context composite tasks across model sizes, not standard downstream benchmarks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
It does not fit scaling exponents or compare fitting choices, loss-curve shapes, or compute-optimal splits.

relationships.reason: Accuracy rises to 96–100% at the largest size in every family (R11, R14, R18, R58). The one dip is Llama2 13B (R13, 74→69).
relationships.display_finding: The largest models in every family reached 96–100% accuracy, although Llama2 13B showed an intermediate decline from 74 to 69.

relationships.condition: Separable task (D)+(F), and compose-by-step tasks (A)+(B) and (B)+(D)
relationships.reason: Gains are non-monotonic within families: Llama1 30B drops to 14% on (D)+(F) (R44), Mistral 8x7B drops (R38), and Llama1 65B falls on (A)+(B) and (B)+(D) (R09, R27). Largest Llama2 and Llama3 models do improve (R05, R23, R56).
relationships.display_finding: Llama1 30B fell to 14% on a separable task, Mistral 8x7B declined, and Llama1 65B declined on stepwise composition tasks, although the largest Llama2 and Llama3 models improved.

relationships.condition: Compose-by-step tasks (G)+(H) and (B)+(E), all families up to 65–70B
relationships.reason: Composite accuracy stays at 0–5% across all sizes (R28–R36, R46–R54). Authors state scaling provides no improvement. For (B)+(E) the simple Opposite task is only about 60%, so floor effects are possible.
relationships.display_finding: Composite accuracy remained at 0–5% across sizes, although approximately 60% accuracy on the simple Opposite task could contribute to floor effects for one composition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Accuracy rises across the reported series for Mistral, Llama1 and Llama3, and rises substantially at the largest Llama2 size; see R10–R18 and R57–R58.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: Scale effects vary by task and model family: several series dip or remain flat, and some arithmetic results stay near zero; see R01–R09, R19–R27, R37–R54.

reader_labels.label: challenges
